dedupe_keys.name: openseamap free nautical chart built on openstreetmap

description: OpenSeaMap is a worldwide open source project, started in 2009, that builds a free nautical chart from nautical information stored in OpenStreetMap. It adds beacons, buoys and other seamarks, port information, repair shops and ship supplies to the OpenStreetMap database, following a seamark tagging schema aligned with the IHO S-57 standard and the newer S-101 standard for electronic navigational charts, and it collects crowd-sourced shallow water depths. The online chart overlays port pilot information, weather forecasts, AIS vessel tracking, gauges and water depths. Coverage is worldwide. The chart can be viewed online free of charge and downloaded for chart plotters, tablets and phones, and the seamark data can be extracted from OpenStreetMap under the ODbL. Caveats: it is volunteer-maintained and not an official chart for navigation, coverage varies by region, and some site news items are years old. The seamark and port data support maritime network models, exposure of ports and navigation aids to storms and sea level rise, and inland waterway studies. It complements the AIS data and the Norwegian maritime traffic data catalogued here.
